summary: John's 4th-great-grand-uncle; coal operator, first president of Kingston borough council (1857), and the likely namesake of Pringle Borough.
bio: Thomas Pringle (2 Nov 1791 - 22 May 1861), eldest son of Samuel and Martha, married Elizabeth Harvey. He mined coal in partnership with his brothers-in-law, is listed among the valley's coal operators around 1843 (Pearce p.380), and in 1837 moved to a large Kingston farm whose lane later became Pringle Street. A county history says Pringle Borough 'takes its name from that of a prominent family of that vicinity' and notes that Thomas Pringle was the first president of Kingston's borough council in 1857; Wikipedia says the borough honours Thomas Pringle. Neither source says which Thomas; another Thomas Pringle, born 1821, also lived in the area.
notable: Likely namesake of Pringle Borough, PA
